html:
The Paraguayan War, or War of the Triple Alliance, was fought from 1864 to 1870 between Paraguay and the alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay. It was the deadliest war between states in the history of Latin America.

Paraguay under Francisco Solano López had a large army and its own arsenal and railway. When Brazil intervened in a civil war in Uruguay in 1864, López saw a threat to the balance of the region. He seized a Brazilian ship, invaded the Brazilian province of Mato Grosso, and then marched through Argentine territory. In 1865 Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay signed a treaty of alliance against him.

The allies won the naval battle of Riachuelo in 1865 but needed years to break the fortress of Humaitá on the Paraguay River, which fell in 1868. Asunción was taken in 1869. López fought on in the hills with a dwindling army of old men and boys until he was killed at Cerro Corá on 1 March 1870.

Paraguay lost much of its population; estimates range from about a quarter to more than half, with men hit hardest. It lost land to Argentina and Brazil. Indigenous peoples of the border lands were drawn in: the Kadiwéu and Terena fought for Brazil in Mato Grosso, and the Guató country in the Pantanal was crossed by armies. After the war the Paraguayan state sold off the Chaco, the land of peoples such as the Enxet.
sum: The Paraguayan War, or War of the Triple Alliance, was fought from 1864 to 1870 between Paraguay and the alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay. It was the deadliest war between states in the history of Latin America.
